from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Standard metrics measure distance on a number line.",
            "Convergence implies getting closer to a limit value.",
            "Small steps result in finite, predictable sums."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Familiar World: Real Convergence", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        number_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 2, 0.2], length=5).shift(DOWN * 1)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(number_line.n2p(0))
        limit_point = Dot(color=RED).move_to(number_line.n2p(1))
        limit_label = Text("Limit (1)", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(limit_point, UP)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title), FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_in_area(number_line, "C2", "C5")
        self.play(Create(number_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        # Move point towards limit
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(limit_point.get_center()), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(FadeIn(limit_point), Write(limit_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["2-adic metrics redefine numerical size.", "Divisibility by two determines 2-adic smallness.", "High powers of two mean smaller values."]
        self.setup_layout("Introducing the 2-adic Metric", lecture_lines)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Infinite sums can diverge in standard calculus.",
            "They behave differently in 2-adic metrics.",
            "Partial sums of powers of two converge.",
            "This series actually approaches negative one.",
            "2-adic space allows non-intuitive convergence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Surprising Sums: Convergence in 2-adic", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6347")) # Tomato
        series = MathTex("1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \\dots", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(series, "B2")
        self.play(Write(series))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#4682B4")) # SteelBlue
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32")) # LimeGreen
        partial_sum = MathTex("S_n = \\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} 2^k = 2^n - 1", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(partial_sum, "C2")
        self.play(FadeIn(partial_sum))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700")) # Gold
        # Showing visual representation of approaching -1 (using |2^n - 1 - (-1)|_2 = |2^n|_2 = 1/2^n -> 0)
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["D2"], end=self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        target_val = MathTex("-1", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(target_val, "D5")
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(target_val))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF69B4")) # HotPink
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "2-adic distances follow the ultrametric inequality.",
            "Triangles behave more like nested hierarchies.",
            "Numerical value is secondary to divisibility."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Key Properties: The Ultrametric Inequality", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"|x + z|_2 \leq \max(|x|_2, |z|_2)")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Represent hierarchy with nested circles
        c1 = Circle(radius=2.0, color=BLUE).set_stroke(width=2)
        c2 = Circle(radius=1.2, color=GREEN).set_stroke(width=2)
        c3 = Circle(radius=0.6, color=RED).set_stroke(width=2)
        
        hierarchy = VGroup(c1, c2, c3)
        self.place_at_grid(hierarchy, "E3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(c1), Create(c2), Create(c3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Label to emphasize divisibility
        div_label = Text("Divisibility Rule", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(div_label, "E5")
        self.play(FadeIn(div_label))

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Distance definitions fundamentally reshape mathematical behavior.",
            "Convergence relies on the underlying metric space.",
            "Different metrics reveal new mathematical truths."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        universe_label = Text("Real Metric", color=BLUE).scale(0.6)
        p_adic_label = Text("2-adic Metric", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6)
        
        standard_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-2, 2], length=4, color=BLUE)
        p_adic_tree = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(5)])
        p_adic_tree.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(standard_line, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(universe_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(standard_line), Write(universe_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(p_adic_tree, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(p_adic_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(p_adic_tree), Write(p_adic_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        final_thought = Text("Mathematical Truth is Contextual", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(final_thought, 'C6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_thought))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently

sections.title: The Familiar World: Real Convergence
sections.content: Establish the prerequisite concept of standard convergence using the Euclidean metric. Visualize a point moving along a number line, getting closer to a limit as steps become smaller in magnitude.
sections.example: A rabbit jumping towards a carrot: each jump is half the distance of the previous one (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... = 1).

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Define the 2-adic valuation |x|_2. Introduce the concept: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by a high power of 2. Use a visual 'tree' or 'fractal' representation where integers branch based on their divisibility by 2.
sections.example: Compare the 'size' of 8 and 1/8. In the 2-adic world, 8 (2^3) is very small (|8|_2 = 1/8), while 1/8 is very large (|1/8|_2 = 8).

sections.title: Surprising Sums: Convergence in 2-adic
sections.content: Show that the series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... (which diverges to infinity in standard calculus) converges in the 2-adic metric. Use a visual animation showing partial sums approaching -1.
sections.example: Think of a binary counter: as you keep adding powers of 2 (1, 10, 100, 1000 in binary), the sum 'fills up' the infinite string to the left, effectively representing -1.

sections.title: Key Properties: The Ultrametric Inequality
sections.content: Explain the Ultrametric Inequality: |x+y|_p ≤ max(|x|_p, |y|_p). Use a graphical 'triangle' to show that 2-adic distances don't behave like standard triangles, but rather like nested boxes or hierarchy levels.
sections.example: A social network graph: if two people share the same 'ancestor' divisible by a high power of 2, they are 'closer' to each other than to anyone else, regardless of the numerical value.

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize how changing the definition of 'distance' changes the behavior of infinite series. Reiterate that convergence is a property of the metric space, not just the numbers.
sections.example: Concluding animation: A 'Parallel Universe' map where the standard number line and the 2-adic tree coexist, showing how different perspectives lead to different mathematical truths.
